title: Passover Seder Checklist (Printable): Seder Plate, Table, Shopping & Timeline
description: A printable Passover seder checklist: what goes on the seder plate, what to put on the table, a shopping list and a countdown from four weeks out to seder night (Passover 2027 begins April 21).
lead: Everything to tick off before the first seder: the countdown, the seder plate, the table and the shopping list. Passover 2027 begins at sundown on Wednesday, April 21, 2027.
body_html:
This is the short, printable version. If it’s your first seder, read how to host a Passover seder first. Ritual items follow the lists published by Chabad.org; customs differ between families and communities, so adapt freely and ask your rabbi about anything halachic.

4–6 weeks before

  • Guest list for each seder (adults / kids), and who brings what.
  • Haggadot: one per guest, ideally the same edition.
  • Shmurah matzah ordered (it can sell out close to the holiday).
  • Menu planned, including any guests’ dietary needs.
  • Kosher-for-Passover wine and grape juice listed (see quantities below).
  • Plan for chametz: what to use up, store or give away.

1–2 weeks before

  • Non-perishable shopping done (matzah, wine, matzo meal, canned goods).
  • Kitchen cleaning plan and dates; kashering plan if you kasher.
  • Extra chairs, table and pillows (for leaning) borrowed.
  • Seder roles assigned: Four Questions, readings, afikoman hunt.
  • Afikoman prize bought.

2–3 days before

  • Fresh shopping: romaine, horseradish, parsley, apples, eggs, produce.
  • Make-ahead cooking: soup, brisket, charoset.
  • Table linens washed; dishes and glasses counted.

The night before

  • Search for chametz (bedikat chametz), if you observe it.
  • Eggs hard-boiled; horseradish grated (keep covered).
  • Shank bone or chicken neck roasted.
  • Salt water mixed (about 1–2 tablespoons of salt in 2 cups of water, per Chabad.org).

The seder plate

  • Zeroa: roasted shank bone or chicken neck.
  • Beitzah: hard-boiled (often roasted) egg.
  • Maror: bitter herbs, usually horseradish and/or romaine.
  • Charoset: apples, nuts and wine, or your family recipe.
  • Karpas: parsley, celery, onion or boiled potato, by custom.
  • Chazeret: second bitter herb (often romaine).

The table

  • Three whole matzot, covered, at the leader’s place (plus matzah for everyone).
  • Wine or grape juice for four cups each.
  • Elijah’s cup (and Miriam’s cup, if your family uses one).
  • Salt water bowls within reach of everyone.
  • A haggadah at every seat.
  • Pillows for leaning at the leader’s seat (or every seat).
  • Candles lit before the holiday begins.
  • Bowl, pitcher and towel for hand-washing.
  • Afikoman wrapped and ready to hide.

How much to buy

Rules of thumb used in our planner (ritual quantities follow Chabad.org’s guidance; meal quantities are catering rules of thumb):

Passover seder quantities
ItemPer adult, per sederNotes
Shmurah matzahabout 2 matzotPlus 3 whole matzot per seder plate
Wineabout ¾ bottleFour cups; grape juice for kids and anyone who prefers it
Eggs1Plus one per seder plate
Romaine (maror)a few leavesAbout one head for 6–7 adults
Brisket (raw)about ½ lbShrinks a lot in cooking

For your exact guest count, use the free seder shopping calculator; it turns adults, kids and number of seders into a shopping list you can print.

Seder night run sheet

Seder night run sheet
WhenWhat
AfternoonTable set; seder plate assembled; wine and juice chilled; afikoman wrapped
1 hour beforeSoup and mains in a low oven; haggadot at each seat; salt water poured
Before sundownCandles lit at the correct time for your location
ArrivalGuests seated; roles reminded (Four Questions, readings)
Kadesh to MaggidFirst cup, karpas, breaking the middle matzah, the story; this is the longest part
Motzi-Matzah to KorechMatzah, maror, the Hillel sandwich; then serve the meal (Shulchan Orech)
After the mealAfikoman found and ransomed, grace after meals, third and fourth cups, songs

Put the soup on the table as soon as Shulchan Orech starts: after an hour of storytelling, hungry guests appreciate speed more than plating.

After the seder

  • Leftover matzah and wine stored for the second seder.
  • Note what ran out and what was left, for next year.
  • Haggadot and seder plate packed together.

Also see: ReformJudaism.org’s hosting checklist and Exploring Judaism’s preparation checklist.

faq.q: What goes on a seder plate?
faq.a: Zeroa (shank bone or chicken neck), beitzah (egg), maror (bitter herbs), charoset, karpas (a vegetable such as parsley or potato) and, in many families, chazeret (a second bitter herb). Customs vary.
Passover 2027 begins at sundown on Wednesday, April 21, 2027, so the first seder is that evening.

faq.q: How much matzah do I need for a seder?
faq.a: Chabad.org's guidance is three whole matzot per seder plate plus about two for each other participant, per seder. Buy extra machine matzah for the meal.

faq.q: How many bottles of wine for a seder?
faq.a: Plan roughly three-quarters of a bottle per adult for the four cups, per seder, plus grape juice for kids.
